body_markdown:
AI call transcription turns customer conversations into searchable text that businesses can review, analyze, and learn from. For customer service teams, it can make it easier to find recurring problems, understand how customers feel, review calls, and spot trends across hundreds or thousands of conversations.


Your customers tell you what they need every day, and AI call transcription helps you use more of what they are already saying to improve the customer experience.


## What is AI call transcription?


AI call transcription uses[artificial intelligence](https://sangoma.com/blog/what-is-ai-call-transcription/) to automatically convert a spoken[phone conversation](https://sangoma.com/products/communications-platform/) into written text. Instead of relying only on a call recording, your business gets a written record that can be searched, reviewed, and analyzed.


Some call transcription software goes further by creating summaries, identifying customer sentiment, and organizing call data for analysis. For customer service teams, this means less time replaying calls to find a specific complaint, question, or detail, while creating a larger record of what customers are asking about across the business.


## Why should businesses pay closer attention to customer calls?


Customer calls are one of the clearest sources of customer feedback because people usually call for a reason, such as getting an answer to a question, solving a problem, making a decision, or asking for something your business may not currently provide.


Paying attention to those conversations can have a real business impact.[Forrester](https://www.forrester.com/bold/customer-obsession/) reports that customer-obsessed organizations have 51% better customer retention than organizations that do not put the same focus on their customers. Research cited by[HubSpot](https://www.hubspot.com/web-guide/the-power-of-smarketing/how-to-develop-a-customer-centric-marketing-strategy) also found that customer-centric companies are 60% more profitable than companies that are not.


The challenge is finding a practical way to learn from customer conversations at scale, especially when your business handles more calls than a person could reasonably review.


## How does AI transcription help customer service teams?


A manager might have time to listen to a handful of recorded calls each week, while AI transcription for customer service calls can make far more conversations available for review.


Automatically transcribing customer calls creates searchable records that managers and teams can use to answer practical questions about the customer experience. They can see what customers are calling about most often, which problems keep coming back, and where people are regularly confused about a product, bill, policy, or process.


AI-generated summaries can also reduce the amount of time spent reviewing individual calls. Instead of replaying a full conversation to understand what happened, a manager can start with the summary and transcript, then return to the recording when more context is needed.


## How can businesses identify customer trends from calls?


A single customer question may not tell you much on its own, but the same question appearing across dozens of calls can point to a larger trend that deserves attention.


This is where AI call transcription can provide a useful starting point for analysis. By turning individual customer conversations into searchable data, it gives managers the information they need to conduct analysis across customers and look for recurring questions, complaints, requests, and other patterns.


A business might discover that customers regularly call because they cannot understand an invoice, while a hotel might see repeated questions about check-in times or a retailer could find that one product is creating more support calls after purchase. These patterns can help businesses decide where they need clearer information, better employee training, product changes, or a different customer process.


## Can AI call transcription help businesses understand customer sentiment?


Transcription gives businesses a written record of what customers said, while sentiment analysis can add context by identifying the general tone of the conversation.


For example,[Sangoma Scribe](https://sangoma.com/products/scribe/) can classify the sentiment of transcriptions as positive, neutral, or negative. Teams can filter calls by sentiment and track those results over time, making it easier to find frustrated customers and look for patterns behind negative conversations.


A rise in negative calls could point to a product, service, billing, or support issue that needs a closer look. Sentiment analysis gives teams another way to find those conversations faster, while employees can review the transcript and recording for the full context.


## What should businesses look for in call transcription software?


Start with how easily the information can fit into your employees’ normal workday. Useful AI transcription should make customer conversations easier to find, review, understand, and act on without creating another complicated process for your team.


[Sangoma Scribe](https://sangoma.com/products/scribe/) automatically transcribes calls and voicemails, creates call summaries, and makes transcripts searchable. It also supports time-synced playback, allowing employees to move from a specific part of the written transcript to the corresponding part of the recording when they need more context.


Reporting can help businesses move from reviewing individual conversations to understanding patterns across many calls. Teams can filter conversations, review sentiment, track trends over time, and search transcripts for specific details, giving managers a clearer view of what customers are experiencing.


For a business owner, the value comes from having a clearer picture of what customers need, where they are running into problems, and where the business has an opportunity to improve.


## Your phone system can become a better source of customer insight


Your customers are already telling you what they like, what frustrates them, what they need help with, and what they may want next. AI call transcription gives your business a practical way to capture more of that information and use it to improve customer service.


Those conversations can help you spot recurring issues, better understand customer needs, and find ways to improve customer service.
